components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action colour: anything the user can press.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #0050D3; color: #fff; padding: 10px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font: 700 14px/1.4 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #003FA7; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #003FA7; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive confirmations such as log out and delete.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: #FF0000; color: #fff; padding: 10px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font: 700 14px/1.4 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #D90000; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B80000; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary actions next to a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: #fff; color: #0050D3; padding: 10px 24px; border: 1px solid #0050D3; border-radius: 8px; font: 700 14px/1.4 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #E6EFFD; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #003FA7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Single-line field with a thin outline and a soft blue focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #E5E5E5; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px 16px; font: 400 14px/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #0A0A0A; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #A3A3A3; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,63,167,0.6); }

components.name: Sidebar Navigation
components.description: Navy rail with white outlined items; the active item fills white.
components.html: DASHBOARDWORKERS
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; background: #012247; padding: 24px; width: 272px; } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 16px; border: 1px solid #fff; border-radius: 8px; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; font: 500 14px/1.4 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-nav-item:hover, .ds-nav-active { background: #fff; color: #012247; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C9DAF8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Round capital label; status colour on its own wash.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-block; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 12px; background: #C9DAF8; color: #012247; font: 700 12px/1.3 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .ds-pill-pending { background: #FEF3E6; color: #B86804; border: 1px solid #FD950F; } .ds-pill-done { background: #E3F4E6; color: #158240; border: 1px solid #1FAA59; }

narrative.overview:
On Call Hub reads like the board on the shop wall: a dark navy frame, a white surface, and every shift pinned up where anyone can see whether it's covered. The design exists to show where a shift stands, at a glance, on a desktop for the owner and on a phone for a worker standing in a queue somewhere. Nothing here is decorative for its own sake; the one warm, playful note is the ice-cream photography and orange greeting on the dashboard hero.

Density is moderate. Content sits in rounded white cards with a thin grey outline and a soft lift, grouped into a single column on phones and two columns (main plus a narrow side rail) on desktop. Headings and labels are set in bold capitals so the board can be scanned from across the room; sentences stay in normal case so they can be read.

Colour carries meaning, not mood. Blue is what you press, orange is what you notice, green is done, red is a problem. Each status also gets a pale wash of its own hue so a whole card or row can be tinted without shouting.
keyCharacteristics: Navy sidebar frame, white working canvas.
Rounded, outlined white cards with a soft shadow.
Bold capital headings and labels; normal-case sentences.
Status shown as colour plus a pale wash of the same hue.

rules.name: The Blue Means Press Rule
rules.body: Action Blue is the only colour for interactive elements. Orange, green and red never appear as a primary button fill; green and red appear on buttons only when the button *is* the status (Approve, Reject, Log out).

rules.name: The Wash Pairing Rule
rules.body: A status colour used as text or outline sits on its own pale wash, never on another hue's wash.

rules.name: The Twelve Pixel Floor
rules.body: No text is smaller than 12px. The incumbent 8–11px sizes are a known defect (OCH-225), not part of the system.

rules.name: The Caps For Names Rule
rules.body: Capitals are for headings, labels, nav items and status pills. Sentences, descriptions, error messages and notification text stay in normal case (OCH-226).

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: A card gets the card lift or nothing; don't stack bigger shadows to make one card louder. Use a wash or an outline colour instead.

dos: Do use Action Blue for anything clickable, and only for that.
Do pair each status colour with its own wash (orange on orange-wash, green on green-wash, red on red-wash, blue on blue-wash).
Do put content in 12px-rounded white cards with a Hairline outline and the card lift.
Do keep all text at 12px or above.
Do set headings, labels, pills and nav items in bold capitals, and keep sentences in normal case.
Do keep the navy sidebar plus white canvas frame on every signed-in page.
Do meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast; check status-colour text on white and on washes before shipping.
donts: Don't use Scoop Orange, green or red as a primary button fill.
Don't set text below 12px (the incumbent 8–11px sizes are being removed in OCH-225).
Don't put whole sentences, error messages or notification text in capitals.
Don't stack heavier shadows to emphasise a card; use a wash or outline colour.
Don't add new one-off hex colours; extend the palette here first.
